problem: Let $A$ be the set of all multiples of $2$ greater than $0$ and let $B$ be the set of all multiples of $3$ greater than $0.$ What is $A∖B?$
worked_solution:
The multiples of $2$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A={2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,18,…}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $3$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B={3,6,9,12,15,18,…}.
$$

Now, $A∖B$ is the *difference* of $A$ and $B,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $A$ but *not* in $B.$

The elements of $A$ that are also in $B$ are $6,12,18,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $6$). So, we must remove these elements from $A.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∖B & =A-B \\  & ={2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,18,…}-{3,6,9,12,15,18,…} \\  & ={2,4,8,10,14,16,…}.\end{aligned}
$$
